text:
maria: Quick heads-up — seeing OOMs on AWQ runs after the kernel-selector flip. Symptoms: OOM during decoding on canary, memory climbs with KV prefetch and then fragmentation spike.

hamid: Which kernel flip exactly? v1->v2 selector? model + seq len?

maria: v1->v2 yes. Example run: mix-llama-awq, seq=1024, batch=3. Pasted a tiny profile from the canary run:

```
runtime.kernel_selector: v2
model: mix-llama-awq
seq_len: 1024
batch_size: 3
allocator: slab
peak_gpu_mem: 21.3GB
oom_point: 20.9GB
kv_cache_dtype: auto-upcast fp16->fp32
prefetch_budget: 128MB
```

darren: I saw similar behavior earlier — allocator's deferred_free window plus small-page fragmentation causes effective usable memory to drop quickly under constant prefetch. Compaction not reclaiming small slices fast enough.

anjali: Two quick ideas: 1) cap prefetch dynamically using a watermark based on free workspace; 2) change KV auto-upcast to lazy-upcast-on-use (avoid full upfront upcast).

maria: Sketch for watermark prefetch throttle:

```
# pseudo
watermark = workspace_total * 0.12  # keep a 12% reserve
if workspace_free < watermark:
  throttle_prefetch()  # reduce concurrent KV fetches
else:
  prefetch_pages(min(prefetch_budget, workspace_free * 0.6))
```

hamid: Also recommend buffer pooling keyed by (dtype, size_class). On kernel flip we often free+alloc same sized buffers with different dtype -> churn. Reuse will reduce alloc calls and fragmentation. Microbench: reuse reduced alloc ops ~72% and fragmentation metric ~13% in local sim.

darren: FYI AWQ per-layer aux tables currently allocate small fp32 scratch for dequant during init, that adds ~200-300MB for large models; compaction of those tables or storing in fp16 where safe could save headroom.

anjali: I'm opening a small PR with two changes: shrink deferred_free window from 500ms -> 100ms for canary, and introduce a dtype-aware pool layer that prefers reuse over free for matching size_class. PR#4521. Running the same canary workload against it now.

maria: Nice. Can we also add a quick fallback rule in the runtime routing: if kernel_selector=v2 and available_workspace_pct < 15% then route to kernel_selector=v1 for that request (canary only)? That avoids breaking user traffic while we iterate.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary/eng-runtime-cluster-3 -> image: runtime:v2026.1-pr4521

hamid: When PR lands we should add a perf test: repeat the AWQ decode job with seq=2048 batch=2 and collect peak+usable memory and fragmentation histogram. Compare baseline vs patched.

darren: noted — also watch for regression on latency tail when we shrink deferred_free; might increase alloc pressure for some kernels. Add a metric: deferred_free_reclaims_per_sec.

maria: I'll wire up token-level memory traces for the canary runs and post graphs to this thread. For now: monitoring alerts set at 1.5x typical peak and will rollback if OOM rate > 0.1% over 30m. :eyes:

anjali: canary run finished — initial numbers look promising: peak down ~350MB, fragmentation index dropped ~9%. Still validating longer jobs.

maria: great. please ping when you have the graphs. thanks all for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
